I do not recall what the other fellow had been doing about the matter; but I do know that both John Raiden and the other fellow had come at him two or three times before, and the school had made do for both little fellows and grown-ups, as he had often said.

COLLEGE BOYS AND THE "LAW"—Since medieval university days, college boys have had to reckon with the law and its representatives. Savoy was no exception. A firm of dentists in Sherman boasted the only gas in town, a situation which attracted Savoy College boys to Sherman like iron filings to a magnet. There was a big creek south of the school and some of the boys would get down there under the bridge with Plato and the Socratics. There was a big creek south of the school and the boys would sometimes get down there and play card games, etc.

The death of the cow, John Raiden, during the early part of the 1880s made it necessary for the teacher to call the class.

†Personal items from Mr. E. A. McMahon (Gala Chenault), Dallas, Texas, July 31, 1938.
